issues.legal_issue: A law specifically included in the constitutional schedule is protected from being held invalid on the ground that it contravenes the earlier constitutional guarantee governing compulsory acquisition of property, including where the challenged provisions had previously been held invalid on that ground.
material_facts: Property was acquired under a law whose compensation provisions contained two provisos limiting how compensation was calculated.
The High Court dismissed the owner's petition but held that the two provisos contravened the earlier constitutional guarantee governing compulsory acquisition of property.
After the High Court's decision, the law was specifically included in the constitutional schedule by a constitutional amendment.
The appeal challenged the part of the High Court's judgment declaring the provisos invalid.
issues.conclusion: The inclusion of the law in the constitutional schedule protected it from being deemed void, or ever to have been void, on the ground that it contravened the earlier constitutional guarantee. The declaration that the provisos were invalid was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-B, read with the Ninth Schedule, provides that listed laws and their provisions are not to be deemed void, or ever to have been void, on the ground that they are inconsistent with or abridge rights in Part III. In Dhirubha Devisingh Gohil v. The State of Bombay, the Court held that the property-acquisition protection in section 299 of the Government of India Act, 1935, was in substance a fundamental right carried into Part III, so Article 31-B protection extends to it. Saghir Ahmad v. The State of U.P. did not apply because the law here was specifically saved by Article 31-B and its inclusion in the Ninth Schedule. Section 5 of the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955, added the law to that Schedule.

predicates.appeal_from_declaration_of_invalidity: An appeal challenges a judgment declaring provisions of a law invalid.
predicates.law_specifically_added_to_protected_sche: The law was specifically added to a constitutional schedule that protects listed laws from invalidity on specified rights-based grounds.
predicates.challenge_based_on_protected_property_ac: The challenge asserts that the law contravenes a constitutional protection governing compulsory acquisition of property.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an invalidity declaration based on the protected property-acquisition right and the law has been specifically added to the protective schedule, the law is not void on that ground.
